title: Safe Hardware Workflow
summary: The Golden Rules of hardware. Keep your components safe from short circuits and static shock.

steps.title: Safety First!
steps.markdownContent:
Unlike software, hardware can be permanently broken if you make a mistake.

Plugging a wire into the wrong place can cause a **short circuit**, instantly destroying an LED or even your Arduino board. You must learn the Safe Hardware Workflow.

steps.title: The First Golden Rule
steps.markdownContent:
**Always unplug your Arduino from USB power before changing any wiring.**

Never pull wires or plug in new components while the green ON light is lit. Build the circuit dead, then bring it to life.

steps.title: The Second Golden Rule
steps.markdownContent:
**Double-check every connection before plugging the USB cable back in.**

Compare your physical breadboard to the Monster Lab diagram. Check the Ground wire, the Power wire, and component orientation (like LED legs). Only plug it in when you are 100% sure.

steps.title: Beware the Static Shock (ESD)
steps.markdownContent:
Have you ever dragged your socks on carpet and shocked a doorknob? That's **Electrostatic Discharge (ESD)**.

While a shock feels tiny to you, it acts like a lightning bolt to an Arduino chip. Always touch a grounded piece of metal (like a metal table leg or computer case) before picking up a bare circuit board to discharge yourself.

steps.markdownContent: Safety is critical. You must get all these questions right to pass.

questions.question: What is the First Golden Rule of wiring?
options: Always unplug power before changing wires
questions.explanation: Never modify a live circuit. Always disconnect power first.

questions.question: What should you do before picking up an Arduino board?
options: Touch a grounded piece of metal to discharge static electricity
questions.explanation: Discharging ESD prevents static shocks from destroying sensitive microchips.

questions.question: When is it safe to plug the USB cable in?
options: Immediately after placing the first part
While you are holding the wires
Only after you have double-checked all connections against the diagram
questions.explanation: Double-check your work first to prevent short circuits upon power-up.
